problem: The text says to wrap the difference into the range (−180°, 180°], but the given formula d = ((v₂ − v₁ + 180) mod 360) − 180 returns −180 for a half-turn (for example 0° to 180° gives −180) and never returns +180. So the stated range contradicts the formula.
fix: State the range as −180° ≤ d < 180°, i.e. (−180°, 180°], said loosely; or describe it as 'a half-turn is taken as a turn of −180°'.

problem: "Easing changes speed, never the path" is stated as an absolute. It holds only when the same easing is applied to every channel of one object. If x and y are eased with different curves (which the chapter itself allows, since each channel has its own keys and rule), the object does not travel the straight line between the two poses, so the spatial path does change.
fix: Add: 'This is true for the single channel being eased. Ease x and y differently and the spatial path itself bends.' Keep the trap, but say it applies to one channel.

problem: A hand reaching for a cup starts from rest and also slows as it arrives, so the motion is slow-in and slow-out. Ease-in alone explains only the start, and the question implies ease-in is the right single choice.
fix: Ask why ease-in is better than linear at the start, and note in the answer that a full reach would use ease-in-out, since the hand also decelerates into the cup.

where: Section 3, final sentence on export frame rate
problem: "Exporting at a frame rate different from the timeline's silently changes how fast everything moves" is only true when keys are stored as frame numbers. Many tools store key times in seconds and resample on export, so the motion keeps its duration.
fix: Say: 'This holds when keys are stored as frame numbers. Tools that store key times in seconds keep the duration and resample instead.'
